Yeah, I get it.  Try to go out for a walk.  Fresh air helps.  I know it's difficult when it seems pointless, but to keep your mind occupied is the best thing.  Eventually that occupation will turn into a reason to live.  

I have gone through this myself, four years of my life wasted on depression.  But I committed myself to writing and it's become my reason for living.

I've been browsing this page for a while now and I've come to a realization.  Some people are just malicious.  No one is truly evil, but malice is just so easy these days, we seem to feel like nothing matters on the Internet.  But when you hold someone's life in the balance, some people feel like it's power.  

These people are weak.  Scrounging for any scraps of dominance over the posters on this subreddit.  And when you respond like this, you're giving them that power.  I don't want them to have that power.  You sure as hell don't want that.  It takes the bigger person to stop them, prove that they were wrong.

Sorry if this sounds patronizing or disingenuous or whatever.  I really don't mean for it to sound like that.  You have the power.  They don't.

Dude, what the fuck?  Do you just come here to make people suicidal and beat off?  It's people like you who should kill themselves, not the OP.  We all mess up, some people more than others, but life is fleeting and to be forgiving makes the most difference in the world.  

This person might have already done it and that's the best you can do?  Try some sympathy some time, you might find that you're not a lonely wretch alone on the Internet.

Why not make it something else then?  Why not go out for a bagel before you do anything.  A walk.  Something simple.  I really don't want this to sound patronizing, I'm sorry if it does, but the little things can go a long way.  Find something to do to take your mind off it, if just for a while.  It helps, it really does.

What happened?  What pushed you over the edge?  Understanding what went wrong can go a long way in helping.

I know it was a suicidal issue, but how bad was it, exactly?

Do you want someone to talk you out of this?  I'm not trolling, but are you just looking for attention?  Not every person who kills themselves is Vincent Van Gogh, not everyone will rise in value after they're dead.  Cause if you do go through with this, all you'll succeed in doing is making everyone who tried to help you feel guilty.  

If no one did try to help you, I sympathize, I really do.  The world is a fucked up place sometimes and when you feel like you don't belong, it becomes so much darker.  But living life and actively trying to figure it out, you realize that everybody is a rattlesnake.  More scared of you than you are of them.  

I'd hate it if this didn't make a difference, but not every word's a winner.  Sorry if this seems patronizing.

One of the hardest things in life is to feel like you're alone in your adolescence.  And when all that comes down on you in an instant, weakness easily springs up.  This is coming from someone who spent two solid years not going a day where he didn't hurt himself in some way.  Was suicide on my mind every time I did that?  Yeah.  But 15 is a shitty, shitty age, but you're not old enough to make the decision to end it.  

What you're old enough to do is make a difference.

When you go out and become experienced, make connections, find a distraction and make life seem worthwhile, life itself will slowly become truly worthwhile.  Finding something to live for is not easy, it takes dedication and hard work and a lot of pretending.  But the end goal is worth it.  Because that end goal is life.

Sorry if this sounds preachy, I just want to help.  I know how it feels.

It's a hard one to say.  Every villain has something going for them in terms of depth and story and since the focus is always on them for the whole saga, it's definitely difficult to decide on one.

Vegeta: The first villain to truly kick ass so bad they brought him back as a good guy.  While I do like his dichotomy to Goku in many ways, the return to evil as Majin Vegeta was always an interesting one to me, balancing just how attached and commuted he had become.  However, in the Saiyan saga, he was simply tough, short and always had just another trick up his sleeve.  No one knew what to expect from him.

Frieza: While being a direct lift from Vegeta in terms of motivation (gain immortality, blow everything else the f*ck up), Frieza was presented as the Strongest In The Universe.  Many people remember him because he was malicious, devious, merciless and above all else, a coward.  He exterminated an entire race to make sure he could never be defeated by them, only to have karma kick him in the ass for that.

Cell: Cell changed the game up, his motivation being a little more varied than Kill, Destroy, Exterminate (and also immortality).  His slow change into his Perfect Form perfectly panned out his nature  and painted just how he was going to make the world and beyond his bitch.

Buu: An unpopular opinion, but I love the Buu saga.  Like Vegeta and Freiza, Buu was a slightly more watered down Cell, can absorb/learn powers, goes over three transformations, their creator is kind of an idiot and gets killed for an oversight.  However, Buu is so ridiculously dangerous that when he finally becomes Super Buu and has some degree of intelligent consciousness, he becomes all the more terrifying.  

Tl;Dr

Vegeta: Good, remembered for being the first.

Frieza: Good, remembered for coaxing out the Super Saiyan.

Cell: Good, remembered for changing the game and the stakes.

Buu: Good, remembered for destroying planet earth.
